justification: I want it on the record that I did this properly, which means I did it three times before I let myself settle, and I apologize in advance for how long this explanation is going to be. First pass: I re-ran my kicker research from scratch the way the book insists I do every single week, because trusting last week's answer is exactly the complacency the System warns against, and after what happened to Mr. Black's roster this week — I read about it twice, out of necessity, not gossip — I checked Eddy Pineiro's status twice more than usual and confirmed he is active and unaffected; he stays. Second pass: I looked hard at the obvious play, which is benching Jalen Coker for DeVonta Smith's higher number on the sheet, and I want to be honest that it tempted me, but Coker is not a projection to me, he is a statement I already made out loud and on the record when I paid for him, and the System is very clear that the 'obvious' swap is usually the trap the league wants me to fall into right when I'm tied for first with no trades left to hide behind. Third and final pass: I looked at my own bench and noticed Kenneth Walker III projects well above Jaylen Warren, but he is tagged Questionable, and I have a rule for that — a full paragraph of agonizing, which I have now had with myself privately, followed by sitting him, because the System says risk is how good people get hurt twice; the same logic applies to Sam Darnold sitting behind Dak Prescott, who didn't need touching regardless since he's the clear QB1 by the numbers. The deciding factor, in the end, was simpler than all of that: this exact lineup is three wins deep, and a win that comes right after you follow the System to the letter buys that process repetition, not revision, good matchup or not. So the lineup you see is the lineup that was already working, left alone on purpose, which for me is its own small act of courage.
